page: Amazon Web Services r5d.2xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, allocating 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system includes 35 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX-512 extensions. Memory provisioning is set at 64 GB of DDR4 RAM, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Unlike diskless R5 variants, the r5d.2xlarge includes a bundled 300 GB NVMe SSD local instance store volume, alongside a 2 Gbps baseline network throughput. No GPUs are attached.

Benchmark testing demonstrates consistent middle-tier performance across memory and caching workloads. The instance achieves 6.82 million Redis SET operations per second and registers 51.22 GB/sec uncached large-block read memory bandwidth. PassMark database operations and multi-core stress testing both place in the middle 50% tier. Conversely, single-threaded processing reflects lower generational performance, with Geekbench single-core scoring 1122.0 and single-threaded gzip compression exhibiting weak results. Large language model inference tasks show weak to poor performance, confirming limited fit for modern generative AI computing.

The presence of high-speed local NVMe storage combined with generous memory capacity makes the instance architecturally efficient for applications bounded by RAM and disk I/O rather than raw CPU clock speeds. Typical workloads include Redis and Memcached caching clusters, relational database read replicas, data transformation staging, and operational logging environments requiring high-speed temporary scratch space.
description: Amazon Web Services r5d.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, it supplies 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores alongside 64 GB of DDR4 RAM, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It integrates a dedicated 300 GB NVMe SSD local instance store, zero GPUs, and a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps. Performance benchmarks indicate reliable middle-tier throughput for memory operations and multi-core processing, achieving 6.82 million Redis SET operations per second and 51.22 GB/sec uncached memory read bandwidth. Conversely, single-thread processing and modern AI model inference demonstrate lower relative throughput. The combination of dense memory allocation and low-latency NVMe scratch storage positions this instance effectively for in-memory databases, Redis caches, real-time data analytics, and intermediate ETL staging tasks where memory capacity and local I/O throughput take precedence over maximum single-core computation speed.
